New rows only: group l2 (behaviour that lever L2 could break) and the measured typing row.  l2 expectations are filled by c255_row_oracles.py (oracles on the preflight world, then table); a table without an `oracle` key is the draft form, in which every mark is NOT-DERIVED.

regression.rule: the 2.5.4 emulator rows are run UNCHANGED on the 2.5.5 Seed medium and must give the 2.5.4 results
regression.sessions: all sessions of c254_rows.py (repl, lib1, oom-rp1, e3, seam, disk-h, reg-repl, reg-disk, reg-ide, reg-oom)

format_change: vs card254-rows-v1: group l2 rows carry expected.script (sessions of key codes through the real (ide NAME) entry, end = exit | abort-idle), expected.checks (reenter-screen, saved-file, buffer-names, repl-value, save-result, stop-text) and optionally expected.prefix_rule; the typing row carries expected.rule (machine-readable pass rule)

session_notes.l2: ONE fresh boot for the whole group is wrong: rows share buffer names (one, two, ev).  Each row starts with (set-symbol-value (quote ide-buffers) nil) as its first REPL step, or runs in its own boot; rows with a RUN/STOP need the stop-probe row first.  Never in the boot of the e3 or seam groups.
session_notes.typing: two boots (control, seed), each on a fresh medium copy; one Xemu at a time; after a STALL of a driver its Xemu can linger: check with pgrep before the next boot, never kill a foreign process

rows.title: MEASURED: editor cost per key (cycles, TAKE to idle), 2.5.5 Seed medium against the 2.5.4 Final medium
steps: boot the control world (2.5.4 Final medium), run the keycost series
boot the 2.5.5 Seed medium, run the same series
rows.expect: insert at column 20 at least 40 % cheaper than 2.5.4 in cycles; Backspace at least 35 % cheaper; Return and the join not slower; no growth with the column or the row beyond 5 %; REPL key cost unchanged
rows.oracle: method of build/card-254-ide-typing-r1/keycost.py (PC breakpoints at TAKE and EMPTY of c2_kernal_event_poll, DWX cycle counter read while stopped, 7 samples per point, median of the samples without a collection); prediction build/card-255-typing-r1/model.json (fit error up to 5.4 %)

expected.metric: cycles from TAKE (inc C2K_INPUT_EVENTS_TAKEN) to the start of the idle wait; 40.5 MHz

seed.name: 2.5.5 Seed r1 [PLACEHOLDER P-SEED: set both hashes from the Seed receipts]

ratio_max: insert at column 20: at least 40 % cheaper
Backspace at column 20: at least 35 % cheaper
insert at column 1: at least 40 % cheaper
insert at column 39: at least 40 % cheaper
Return at the end of a 30-character line: not slower
Backspace joining two lines: not slower
growth_max: no growth with the column (39 against 1)
no growth with the row (line 20 against line 1, column 10)
unchanged: REPL insert unchanged (native code is byte-identical)
control_reference: the method reproduces the 2.5.4 measurement on the control world
burst: burst of 32: step per coalesced key not slower, ONE render
prediction: insert at column 20 against the model
Backspace at column 20 against the model
Return at column 30 against the model

rule_text: FAIL: any ratio / growth / unchanged / control-reference / burst rule, a key that is not rendered, fewer than 7 samples, a point with fewer than 3 samples within 2 % of its median (samples with a collection excluded; 2.5.4 had 3 to 7), a missing point, or more collections in the single editor keys than the control run
REVIEW (no automatic pass, no fail): a measured point more than 15 % away from the model prediction -- the gain is real but the model is wrong; explain before the ship
PASS: everything else.  Thresholds are a proposal; they are a reviewer decision (D-TIME)

derivation.why: emulator measurement; the host gives VM instruction counts and the model only

host_first: the whole row; real hardware timing is not modelled (keyboard matrix scan, repeat)
rows.status_rule: MEASURED row: status = the verdict of c255_row_oracles.py timing; the control run is part of the row
